mock_data.title: Ancestral Voices
mock_data.passage:
A New Scientist book review by Peter Hoskin of Proto by Laura Spinney, about hunting the origins of Proto-Indo-European, the ancestor of many modern languages.

A new book by Laura Spinney is rather tantalisingly called Proto, begging the question: proto-what? Prototype, the earliest version of a technology? Protoplasm, the stuff of our cells? Or even protoplanet, a small hunk of space rock with a big future ahead?

The answer, in fact, sits above and across those words: Proto-Indo-European. This is the great original language from which English, among many other tongues, both alive and dead, derives. As Spinney puts it: "Almost every second person on Earth speaks Indo-European." And the task she has set herself in Proto: How one ancient language went global is to explain how.

The story she ends up telling, through a mixture of reportage and beautiful prose, is one that spans millennia, dozens of civilisations and thousands of kilometres. It is a magisterial feat.

It starts around the swirling waters of the Black Sea, about 6000 to 7000 years ago, where ancient peoples started meeting, merging and mimicking each other's vocabularies to achieve goals such as trade.

Encompassing modern-day countries such as Ukraine and Bulgaria, this area was and is so rich in resources that it became a foundry for the Copper Age and many other developments. It is from here that the steppe folk reckoned to be the source of Proto-Indo-European – known as the Yamna in Ukrainian and the Yamnaya in Russian – struck out.

The Yamna are long gone, as is the language they spoke. They belong to prehistory, before written records began. This makes the early chapters of Proto a model of educated imagination. Here, drawing on the available evidence, Spinney allows the Yamna to live again. They aren't just skeletons, but fully fleshed people who stood around 1.8 metres tall, drank milk and smoked cannabis. They had, it is thought, a word for "wheel" (k'ék'los) and another for "honey" (mélit).

If all that makes Proto sound too much like a history book, then rest assured: there is a lot of science going on. Spinney, who has written features for New Scientist, explains that the study of Proto-Indo-European and its proliferation is a multidisciplinary pursuit. There is linguistics, enabling researchers to work backwards through various languages, grabbing on to roots of roots of roots, before having a go at reconstructing Proto-Indo-European itself (and those words for wheel and honey are reconstructions).

Then there is archaeology, which enables us to see the Yamna's journeys through time and space. And there is genetics, by which we can track their advances through other populations. According to one study Spinney cites, "migrants had radiated east and west from the steppe around five thousand years ago, and in Europe their ancestry had replaced up to ninety per cent or more of the gene pool".

Migration is a huge part of Spinney's story. After the initial explications of Proto-Indo-European and the Yamna, the book effectively becomes a chapter-by-chapter account of migrations, large and small, violent and peaceful, by which the original language spread and split.

There are 12 main branches of Proto-Indo-European – from Greek to Germanic, Italic to Indic – all of which divide into branches of their own. Some of those have withered and died. As Spinney recounts in one of the most evocative passages of Proto, the disappeared Tocharian, found along the routes of China's Silk Road, may have been the result of an ambitious, one-off trek by the Yamna centuries before.

It is in these chapters that Proto can get a little knotty. You need to keep your brain switched on to distinguish between Hittites and Hattians or between one chromosomal group and another. Spinney shares every side of every argument to a fault: sometimes you are just getting to grips with a complicated idea when another is suddenly thrust upon you.

Yet such are the demands of the vanished past and its vanished languages. Any book that offers certainty on prehistory ought to be disregarded. Proto doesn't do that. It is clever, careful, expansive, insightful and a host of other fine Indo-European adjectives.
mock_data.passageB1:
Laura Spinney has written a new book called Proto. The name makes you wonder what it means. Is it like a prototype, which is the first version of something new? Or maybe like protoplasm, the material that makes up our cells? Or even a protoplanet, a small rock in space that might become a planet?

Actually, "Proto" refers to Proto-Indo-European. This is a very old language. Many languages we speak today, like English, come from it. Spinney says that almost half the people in the world speak a language that comes from Proto-Indo-European. In her book, Proto: How one ancient language went global, she wants to explain how this happened.

The story she tells is about thousands of years, many different civilizations, and a very large area of land. It's a big and impressive story.

It begins near the Black Sea, about 6000 to 7000 years ago. In that area, people started to meet and mix together. They also started to copy words from each other to help them do things like trade.

The area includes countries like Ukraine and Bulgaria today. It was a place with many resources, so it became important for new ideas and inventions, like the Copper Age. From this area, the steppe people, who are thought to have spoken Proto-Indo-European, began to move to other places. These people are called the Yamna in Ukrainian and Yamnaya in Russian.

The Yamna people are gone now, and so is their language. They lived before people started writing things down. So, the first part of Spinney's book uses imagination based on what we know. She uses the evidence we have to make the Yamna people seem real again. They are not just bones, but people who were tall, drank milk, and even smoked cannabis. They probably had a word for "wheel" (k'ék'los) and another word for "honey" (mélit).

The book is not just about history. There is also a lot of science in it. Spinney explains that studying Proto-Indo-European is a job that needs many different skills. It uses linguistics, which helps researchers look back at different languages to find the oldest parts. This helps them to reconstruct Proto-Indo-European. The words for “wheel” and “honey” are examples of words that have been reconstructed.

It also uses archaeology, which helps us see where the Yamna people went. And it uses genetics, which helps us follow them through other groups of people. One study says that these people moved from the steppe about 5000 years ago. In Europe, they changed the gene pool of the people there by a large amount.

Migration, or people moving from one place to another, is a big part of Spinney's story. After she explains about Proto-Indo-European and the Yamna, the book tells about different movements of people. These movements were sometimes big and sometimes small, sometimes violent and sometimes peaceful. This is how the language spread and changed.

There are 12 main parts, or branches, of Proto-Indo-European. These include Greek, Germanic, Italic, and Indic. Each of these parts then divides into smaller parts. Some of these smaller parts have disappeared. For example, the Tocharian language, which was found along the Silk Road in China, might have been from a single trip by the Yamna people long ago.

In these parts of the book, it can be a little hard to follow. You need to pay attention to the difference between groups of people or groups of chromosomes. Spinney explains every detail of every idea. Sometimes, just when you understand something, she gives you another idea to think about.

But this is because the past and old languages are complicated. Any book that says it knows everything about prehistory is probably wrong. Proto doesn't do that. It is clever, careful, big, and insightful.

mock_data.passageC1:
Laura Spinney's latest offering, provocatively titled Proto, immediately begs the question of its referent. Is it a prototype, the nascent iteration of a technological marvel? Perhaps protoplasm, the fundamental substance of life itself? Or even a protoplanet, a cosmic fragment pregnant with celestial potential?

The answer, however, transcends and encompasses these possibilities: Proto-Indo-European. This is the fountainhead from which English, alongside a multitude of other languages, both extant and extinct, ultimately descends. As Spinney succinctly puts it, "Almost every second person on Earth speaks Indo-European." The ambitious undertaking she sets forth in Proto: How one ancient language went global is to elucidate the mechanisms of this linguistic dissemination.

The narrative that Spinney masterfully constructs, through a blend of meticulous reportage and elegant prose, traverses millennia, encompassing scores of civilizations and spanning vast geographical expanses. It represents a truly magisterial achievement.

The story unfolds around the Black Sea's turbulent shores, approximately 6000 to 7000 years ago, where ancient communities began to interact, integrate, and assimilate each other's linguistic elements, driven by pragmatic objectives such as facilitating trade.

This region, encompassing contemporary Ukraine and Bulgaria, was – and remains – exceptionally resource-rich, serving as a crucible for the Copper Age and numerous subsequent advancements. It is from this area that the steppe peoples, widely considered the originators of Proto-Indo-European – known as the Yamna in Ukrainian and the Yamnaya in Russian – embarked on their migrations.

The Yamna have long since vanished, as has their language. They reside in the realm of prehistory, preceding the advent of written records. This necessitates a degree of informed speculation in the early chapters of Proto. Drawing upon the available evidence, Spinney reanimates the Yamna, presenting them not merely as skeletal remains, but as fully realized individuals, approximately 1.8 meters tall, consuming milk and even partaking in cannabis use. They are believed to have possessed words for "wheel" (k'ék'los) and "honey" (mélit), both meticulously reconstructed.

Lest this portrayal give the impression that Proto is solely a historical treatise, it is important to emphasize the significant scientific underpinning. Spinney, a seasoned contributor to New Scientist, elucidates that the study of Proto-Indo-European and its proliferation is an inherently multidisciplinary endeavor. It incorporates linguistics, enabling researchers to trace languages backward, meticulously identifying the etymological roots from which they originate, before attempting to reconstruct Proto-Indo-European itself (those words for wheel and honey being prime examples of such reconstruction).

Archaeology provides the context for understanding the Yamna's movements through time and space. And genetics allows us to trace their impact on other populations. According to a study cited by Spinney, "migrants had radiated east and west from the steppe around five thousand years ago, and in Europe their ancestry had replaced up to ninety per cent or more of the gene pool".

Migration constitutes a central theme in Spinney's narrative. Following the initial exposition of Proto-Indo-European and the Yamna, the book essentially becomes a series of case studies, chronicling the diverse migrations – large and small, violent and peaceful – through which the original language disseminated and diversified.

There are 12 primary branches of Proto-Indo-European – ranging from Greek to Germanic, Italic to Indic – each of which subsequently subdivides into its own constituent branches. Some of these have atrophied and disappeared entirely. As Spinney recounts in one of the most evocative passages of Proto, the extinct Tocharian language, discovered along the Silk Road in China, may have been the consequence of a single, ambitious expedition undertaken by the Yamna centuries prior.

It is within these later sections that Proto can become somewhat convoluted. Sustained mental agility is required to differentiate between Hittites and Hattians, or between distinct chromosomal groups. Spinney presents every facet of every argument, almost to a fault; just as one begins to grasp a complex concept, another is immediately introduced. Nevertheless, such is the nature of grappling with the vanished past and its extinct languages. Any book purporting to offer absolute certainty regarding prehistory should be treated with skepticism. Proto avoids this pitfall. It is insightful, expansive, meticulous, clever, and a wealth of other laudable Indo-European adjectives.

mock_data.translation:
Peter Hoskin tomonidan yozilgan New Scientist kitob sharhi — Laura Spinneyning ko'plab zamonaviy tillarning ajdodi bo'lgan Proto-Hind-Yevropa tilining kelib chiqishini izlash haqidagi Proto kitobi haqida.

Laura Spinneyning yangi kitobi juda qiziqarli tarzda Proto deb nomlangan, bu savol tug'diradi: proto-nima? Prototip, texnologiyaning eng dastlabki versiyasi? Protoplazma, hujayralarimiz moddasi? Yoki hatto protoplanleta, katta kelajagi bor kichik kosmik tosh bo'lagi?

Javob, aslida, o'sha so'zlarning tepasida va bo'ylab joylashgan: Proto-Hind-Yevropa. Bu ingliz tili, boshqa ko'plab tirik va o'lik tillar kelib chiqqan buyuk asl tildir. Spinney aytganidek: "Yer yuzidagi deyarli har ikkinchi odam Hind-Yevropa tilida gaplashadi." Va u Proto: Bir qadimiy til qanday qilib global bo'ldi kitobida o'ziga qo'ygan vazifa buni tushuntirishdir.

U aytib beradigan hikoya, reportaj va go'zal nasrning aralashmasi orqali, ming yilliklarni, o'nlab sivilizatsiyalarni va minglab kilometrlarni qamrab oladi. Bu ulug'vor yutuqdir.

Bu Qora dengizning girdobli suvlari atrofida, taxminan 6000 dan 7000 yil oldin boshlanadi, u yerda qadimiy xalqlar savdo kabi maqsadlarga erishish uchun bir-birining lug'atlarini uchrashtirib, birlashtira va taqlid qila boshladilar.

Ukraina va Bolgariya kabi zamonaviy mamlakatlarni qamrab olgan bu hudud resurslar jihatidan juda boy bo'lgan va shunday qolgan, shuning uchun u Mis davri va boshqa ko'plab yutuqlar uchun asos bo'lgan. Proto-Hind-Yevropa tilining manbai hisoblangan cho'l xalqlari – ukraincha Yamna va ruscha Yamnaya deb atalgan – shu yerdan yo'lga chiqqan.

Yamnalar allaqachon yo'q bo'lib ketgan, ular gapiradigan til ham shunday. Ular yozma yozuvlar boshlanishidan oldingi tarixdan oldingi davrga tegishli. Bu Protoning dastlabki boblarini ta'limli tasavvurning namunasiga aylantiradi. Bu yerda, mavjud dalillarga tayangan holda, Spinney Yamnalarga qayta hayot beradi. Ular faqat skeletlar emas, balki bo'yi taxminan 1,8 metr, sut ichgan va kanabis chekkan to'la gavdali odamlardir. Ular, deb hisoblanadi, "g'ildirak" uchun so'z (k'ék'los) va "asal" uchun boshqa so'zga (mélit) ega edi.

Agar bularning barchasi Protoni juda ko'p tarix kitobiga o'xshatsa, ishonch hosil qiling: juda ko'p fan bor. New Scientist uchun maqolalar yozgan Spinney Proto-Hind-Yevropa va uning tarqalishini o'rganish ko'p fanli mashg'ulot ekanligini tushuntiradi. Tilshunoslik bor, bu tadqiqotchilarga turli tillar orqali orqaga ishlash, ildizlarning ildizlarining ildizlarini ushlash va keyin Proto-Hind-Yevropa tilini qayta qurishga urinish imkonini beradi (va g'ildirak va asal uchun so'zlar qayta qurishlardir).

Keyin arxeologiya bor, bu bizga Yamnalarning vaqt va makondagi sayohatlarini ko'rish imkonini beradi. Va genetika bor, uning yordamida boshqa populatsiyalar orqali ularning yutuqlarini kuzatishimiz mumkin. Spinney keltirgan bitta tadqiqotga ko'ra, "muhojirlar taxminan besh ming yil oldin cho'ldan sharqqa va g'arbga tarqalgan va Yevropada ularning ajdodlari gen fondining to'qson foiz yoki undan ko'prog'ini almashtirgan".

Migratsiya Spinney hikoyasining katta qismi. Proto-Hind-Yevropa va Yamnaning dastlabki tushuntirishlaridan so'ng, kitob samarali ravishda asl til tarqalgan va bo'lingan katta va kichik, zo'ravon va tinch migratsiyalarning bob-bob hikoyasiga aylanadi.

Proto-Hind-Yevropa tilining 12 ta asosiy tarmog'i bor – Yunon tilidan Germancha, Italikdan Hindikgacha – ularning barchasi o'z navbatida tarmoqlarga bo'linadi. Ularning ba'zilari so'ligan va o'lgan. Spinney Protoning eng ta'sirchan parchalaridan birida hikoya qilganidek, Xitoyning Ipak yo'li yo'nalishlari bo'ylab topilgan yo'q bo'lib ketgan Toxar tili, asrlar oldin Yamnalarning shuhratparast, bir martalik safar natijasi bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkin.

Bu boblarda Proto biroz murakkablashishi mumkin. Xettlar va Xattianlar yoki bitta xromosoma guruhi va boshqasi o'rtasida farqlash uchun miyangizni faol tutishingiz kerak. Spinney har bir bahsning har bir tomonini haddan tashqari baham ko'radi: ba'zan siz murakkab g'oyani endigina tushuna boshlaganingizda, boshqasi to'satdan oldingizga kelib tushadi.

Ammo yo'q bo'lib ketgan o'tmish va uning yo'q bo'lib ketgan tillari shunday talablar qo'yadi. Tarixdan oldingi davr haqida aniqlik taklif qiladigan har qanday kitobni e'tiborsiz qoldirish kerak. Proto bunday qilmaydi. U aqlli, ehtiyotkor, keng qamrovli, chuqur va boshqa ko'plab ajoyib Hind-Yevropa sifatlarining mezboni.

mock_data.translationB1:
Laura Spinney Proto deb nomlangan yangi kitob yozdi. Bu nom sizni uning ma'nosi haqida o'ylantiradi. U yangi narsaning birinchi versiyasi bo'lgan prototipga o'xshashmi? Yoki hujayralarimizni tashkil etuvchi material bo'lgan protoplazmaga o'xshashmi? Yoki hatto sayyoraga aylanishi mumkin bo'lgan kosmosdagi kichik tosh bo'lgan protoplanetaga o'xshashmi?

Aslida, "Proto" Proto-Hind-Yevropa tiliga ishora qiladi. Bu juda qadimgi til. Biz bugun gaplashadigan ko'plab tillar, masalan, ingliz tili, undan kelib chiqqan. Spinneyning aytishicha, dunyo aholisining deyarli yarmi Proto-Hind-Yevropa tilidan kelib chiqqan tilda gaplashadi. U o'zining Proto: Qanday qilib bir qadimiy til global bo'ldi kitobida buning qanday sodir bo'lganini tushuntirmoqchi.

U aytib bergan hikoya ming yillar, turli xil sivilizatsiyalar va juda katta yer maydoni haqida. Bu katta va ta'sirchan hikoya.

U taxminan 6000-7000 yil oldin Qora dengiz yaqinida boshlanadi. O'sha hududda odamlar uchrashib, aralasha boshladilar. Ular, shuningdek, savdo kabi ishlarni bajarishga yordam berish uchun bir-birlaridan so'zlarni nusxalashni boshladilar.

Hududga bugungi Ukraina va Bolgariya kabi mamlakatlar kiradi. U ko'plab resurslarga ega bo'lgan joy edi, shuning uchun u mis davri kabi yangi g'oyalar va ixtirolar uchun muhim bo'lib qoldi. Ushbu hududdan Proto-Hind-Yevropa tilida gaplashgan deb hisoblangan dasht xalqlari boshqa joylarga ko'chib o'ta boshladilar. Bu odamlar ukrain tilida Yamna, rus tilida esa Yamnaya deb ataladi.

Yamna xalqi endi yo'q, ularning tili ham yo'q. Ular odamlar yozishni boshlashidan oldin yashagan. Shunday qilib, Spinney kitobining birinchi qismi biz bilgan narsalarga asoslangan tasavvurdan foydalanadi. U Yamna xalqini yana haqiqiy ko'rsatish uchun bizda mavjud bo'lgan dalillardan foydalanadi. Ular shunchaki suyaklar emas, balki bo'yi baland, sut ichgan va hatto kannabis chekkan odamlar edi. Ularda ehtimol "g'ildirak" (k'ék'los) va "asal" (mélit) uchun so'z bo'lgan.

Kitob faqat tarix haqida emas. Unda ko'plab fan ham bor. Spinneyning ta'kidlashicha, Proto-Hind-Yevropa tilini o'rganish ko'plab turli xil ko'nikmalarni talab qiladigan ishdir. U eng qadimgi qismlarni topish uchun tadqiqotchilarga turli tillarga nazar tashlashga yordam beradigan lingvistikadan foydalanadi. Bu ularga Proto-Hind-Yevropani tiklashga yordam beradi. "G'ildirak" va "asal" so'zlari tiklangan so'zlarga misoldir.

U, shuningdek, Yamna xalqi qayerga ketganini ko'rishga yordam beradigan arxeologiyadan foydalanadi. Va u ularni boshqa odamlar guruhlari orqali kuzatishga yordam beradigan genetikadan foydalanadi. Bir tadqiqotga ko'ra, bu odamlar taxminan 5000 yil oldin dashtdan ko'chib o'tgan. Yevropada ular u yerdagi odamlarning gen fondini katta miqdorda o'zgartirdilar.

Migratsiya, yoki odamlarning bir joydan boshqa joyga ko'chishi, Spinney hikoyasining katta qismidir. U Proto-Hind-Yevropa va Yamna haqida tushuntirgandan so'ng, kitob odamlarning turli xil harakatlari haqida hikoya qiladi. Bu harakatlar ba'zan katta, ba'zan kichik, ba'zan zo'ravonlik bilan, ba'zan tinch bo'lgan. Til shu tarzda tarqaldi va o'zgardi.

Proto-Hind-Yevropaning 12 ta asosiy qismi yoki tarmoqlari mavjud. Bularga grek, german, italyan va hind tillari kiradi. Ushbu qismlarning har biri keyin kichikroq qismlarga bo'linadi. Ushbu kichik qismlarning ba'zilari yo'q bo'lib ketgan. Misol uchun, Xitoydagi Ipak yo'li bo'ylab topilgan Toxar tili, Yamna xalqining uzoq vaqtdagi bir martalik sayohati natijasi bo'lishi mumkin.

Kitobning ushbu qismlarida kuzatib borish biroz qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Odamlar guruhlari yoki xromosomalar guruhlari o'rtasidagi farqga e'tibor berishingiz kerak. Spinney har bir g'oyaning har bir detalini tushuntiradi. Ba'zan, nimanidir tushunganingizda, u sizga o'ylash uchun yana bir g'oya beradi.

Ammo buning sababi shundaki, o'tmish va qadimgi tillar murakkab. Tarixdan oldingi davr haqida hamma narsani bilaman degan har qanday kitob, ehtimol, noto'g'ri bo'ladi. Proto bunday qilmaydi. U aqlli, ehtiyotkor, katta va teran.
mock_data.translationB2:
Laura Spinneyning yangi kitobi, Proto, sarlavhasi sizni o'ylantirib qo'yadi: proto-nima? Bu prototip haqidami, masalan, yangi gadjetning birinchi versiyasi? Yoki balki protoplazma, tirik hujayralarning asosiy moddasi? Yoki hatto protoplaneta, hali shakllanayotgan kichik planeta?

Aslida, javob bularning hammasidan kattaroq: Proto-Hind-Yevropa. Bu ko'plab tillarning, ham eski, ham yangi, shu jumladan ingliz tilining asosiy tili. Spinney yozganidek, "Dunyoda deyarli yarmi Hind-Yevropa tilida gaplashadi." Proto: Qanday qilib bir qadimiy til globalga aylandi kitobida u buni qanday sodir bo'lganini tushuntirishga harakat qiladi.

U hikoya qilgan voqea, ham reportaj, ham tavsifiy yozuvdan foydalangan holda, ming yillar, ko'plab madaniyatlar va ulkan masofalarni qamrab oladi. Bu haqiqatan ham ta'sirchan yutuq.

U taxminan 6000 dan 7000 yil oldin Qora dengiz atrofida boshlanadi. Ushbu hududda qadimiy odamlar uchrasha boshladilar, aralashdilar va bir-birlaridan so'zlar o'zlashtirdilar, ko'pincha savdo maqsadlarida.

Bugungi kunda Ukraina va Bolgariya kabi davlatlarni o'z ichiga olgan bu mintaqa resurslarga boy edi. U mis davri va boshqa yutuqlar markaziga aylandi. Bu yerdan Proto-Hind-Yevropa manbai deb hisoblangan dasht xalqi – Yamna nomi bilan mashhur – tarqala boshladi.

Yamna xalqi va ularning tili uzoq o'tmishda qolgan. Ular yozma yozuvlar mavjud bo'lishidan oldin yashagan. Bu Proto ning dastlabki qismlarini asosli taxminning yaxshi namunasi qiladi. Spinney Yamnani hayotga qaytarish uchun mavjud dalillardan foydalanadi. Ular shunchaki skeletlar emas; ular bo'yi taxminan 1,8 metr bo'lgan, sut ichgan va kannabis chekkan haqiqiy odamlar. Ularda "g'ildirak" (k'ék'los) va "asal" (mélit) uchun so'z bo'lgan deb ishoniladi.

Agar bu Proto ni shunchaki tarix kitobiga o'xshatsa, xavotir olmang: unda ko'plab fanlar mavjud. New Scientist uchun maqolalar yozgan Spinney, Proto-Hind-Yevropani o'rganish va uning tarqalishi ko'plab turli sohalarni talab qilishini tushuntiradi. U yerda tilshunoslik bor, bu tadqiqotchilarga tillarni o'z ildizlariga qaytishga va Proto-Hind-Yevropaning o'zini rekonstruksiya qilishga urinishga imkon beradi. G'ildirak va asal uchun bu so'zlar rekonstruksiyalardir.

Keyin arxeologiya bor, bu bizga Yamnaning vaqt va makondagi harakatlarini ko'rishga yordam beradi. Va genetika bor, bu bizga ularning boshqa populyatsiyalarga ta'sirini kuzatishga imkon beradi. Spinney tilga olgan bir tadqiqotga ko'ra, "migrantlar taxminan besh ming yil oldin dashtdan sharq va g'arbga tarqalgan va Evropada ularning ajdodlari gen fondining to'qson foizdan ko'prog'ini almashtirgan."

Migratsiya Spinney hikoyasining asosiy qismidir. Proto-Hind-Yevropa va Yamnani tushuntirgandan so'ng, kitob migratsiyalarning bir qator hisoblariga aylanadi, ham katta, ham kichik, zo'ravonliksiz va tinch, ular orqali asl til rivojlandi va ajraldi.

Proto-Hind-Yevropaning 12 ta asosiy tarmog'i mavjud – yunonchadan german, italikdan hind – ularning har birining o'z shoxlari bor. Ularning ba'zilari yo'q bo'lib ketgan. Spinney Proto ning eng esda qolarli qismlaridan birida ta'riflaganidek, Xitoydagi Ipak yo'li bo'ylab topilgan Toxar tili, asrlar oldin Yamnaning yagona, ambitsiyali sayohatining natijasi bo'lishi mumkin.

Ushbu qismlarda Proto ni tushunish biroz qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Xetlar va Xattlar, yoki turli xromosomal guruhlari o'rtasida farq qilish uchun diqqat bilan e'tibor berishingiz kerak. Spinney har bir argumentning har bir tomonini batafsil bayon qiladi. Ba'zan, siz bir murakkab g'oyani tushuna boshlaganingizda, yana biri sizga tashlanadi.

Biroq, bu uzoq o'tmish va uning yo'qolgan tillari bilan shug'ullanganda zarurdir. Tarixdan oldingi davr haqida aniqlikni taklif qiladigan har qanday kitobga shubha bilan qarash kerak. Proto buni qilmaydi. U aqlli, ehtiyotkor, mukammal, chuqur va boshqa ko'plab ijobiy sifatlarga ega.

Proto-Hind-Yevropa va Yamna haqidagi dastlabki bayonotdan so‘ng, kitob, asosan, asl til tarqalgan va diversifikatsiya qilingan turli migratsiyalarni - katta va kichik, zo‘ravon va tinch - xronikalashtiruvchi bir qator keys tadqiqotlariga aylanadi.

Proto-Hind-Yevropaning 12 ta asosiy tarmog‘i mavjud - yunondan german, italyandan hindga qadar - ularning har biri keyinchalik o‘zining tarkibiy tarmoqlariga bo‘linadi. Ularning ba’zilari atrofiyaga uchradi va butunlay yo‘q bo‘lib ketdi. Spinney Protoning eng hayajonli parchalaridan birida hikoya qilganidek, Xitoydagi Ipak yo‘lida topilgan yo‘q bo‘lib ketgan Toxar tili Yamna tomonidan asrlar oldin amalga oshirilgan bitta ambitsioz ekspeditsiyaning natijasi bo‘lishi mumkin.

Aynan shu keyingi bo‘limlarda Proto biroz chalkash bo‘lishi mumkin. Xetlar va Xattlar o‘rtasida yoki xromosomalarning alohida guruhlari o‘rtasida farq qilish uchun doimiy aqliy chaqqonlik talab etiladi. Spinney har bir argumentning har bir jihatini deyarli xatoga yo‘l qo‘ymaslik uchun taqdim etadi; murakkab tushunchani tushuna boshlaganingizda, darhol boshqasi kiritiladi. Shunga qaramay, bu yo‘q bo‘lib ketgan o‘tmish va uning yo‘q bo‘lib ketgan tillari bilan kurashishning mohiyatidir. Tarixdan oldingi davrga nisbatan mutlaq ishonchni taklif qiluvchi har qanday kitobga shubha bilan qarash kerak. Proto bu xatodan qochadi. U chuqur, keng qamrovli, puxta, aqlli va boshqa maqtovga sazovor hind-yevropa sifatlariga boy.
